- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/SinTan1729/chhoto-url
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
7	  port: 4567
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: none. This app stores its links in SQLite on a volume and speaks no other database; deploy_compose already defaults to database 'compose', which is correct here
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: chhoto-url
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ UPSTREAM'S SHIPPED compose.yaml DOES NOT PARSE. DO NOT COPY IT. Two separate defects, both measured by running docker compose config against the committed file (Docker 29.6.2, 2026-08-17), and either one alone stops the stack before a single image is pulled. FIRST: the WAL option is written with spaces around the equals sign, which makes the variable NAME carry a trailing space; compose refuses the file with 'environment variable CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE  is declared with a trailing space'. On any engine lenient enough to accept it, the app would look for a name it never sees and WAL mode would be silently off, which is the worse outcome of the two. SECOND, after fixing that: 'service chhoto-url refers to undefined volume data: invalid compose project', because the service mounts data:/data while the top-level volumes block declares db. Use the corrected compose written out in the body of this file, and write environment as a MAP rather than a list of strings so this whole class of bug cannot recur."
18	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. THE ADMINISTRATOR IS WHOEVER KNOWS CHHOTO_PASSWORD, AND YOU SET IT AT DEPLOY TIME. That is the safe-by-construction case, so there is no first-visitor race to lose. It is also the ONLY thing standing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. Verified in backend/src/auth.rs:112-115: is_session_valid begins 'If there's no password provided, just return true', so with an unset or empty password EVERY anonymous request is a valid admin session, with listing, editing and deletion. config.rs:221-226 filters an empty string out too, and the only signal is one warn line at boot, 'No password was provided. The API will be accessible to the public.' GENERATE A LONG ALPHANUMERIC PASSWORD, pass it as CHHOTO_PASSWORD, and verify with the whoami check in the body of this file BEFORE handing over the URL. There is no registration to close afterwards, ever: the README's 'Bloat that will not be implemented' section rules out user management by design."
19	  - "⛔ THE SHIPPED COMPOSE ALSO CARRIES A PUBLICLY DOCUMENTED PASSWORD, UNDER THE LEGACY VARIABLE NAME. Its environment block sets the old lowercase name to a value printed in their public repo, and that value still works: config.rs:41-51 falls back from CHHOTO_PASSWORD to the legacy lowercase name and merely warns 'consider updating your configs'. So a copy-paste deploy is an instance whose admin password is in a file anyone can read on GitHub. Use the NEW names (every variable is CHHOTO_-prefixed at 7.5.0) and your own generated value. The verification script in the body of this file probes the shipped one on purpose, because a wrong-password 401 is the only thing that proves your value is actually the one in force."
20	  - "⛔⛔ A URL SHORTENER ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS A SPAM AND PHISHING REDIRECT SERVICE THE MOMENT ANYONE ELSE CAN POST TO IT, AND THE COST LANDS ON THE HOSTNAME RATHER THAN ON WHOEVER ABUSED IT. Campaigns hunt for exactly this: an open shortener on a domain with a clean reputation. Within days the hostname is in Google Safe Browsing, the DNS blocklists and the corporate URL filters, and a *.redu.cloud name carries reputation other people share. Chhoto URL has NO destination screening of any kind: there is no blocklist, no reputation check and no report flow anywhere in the codebase, which is deliberate, since the README's own 'Bloat' section rules out that class of feature. So KEEP CHHOTO_PUBLIC_MODE OFF. It is off by default (config.rs reads it as enabled only on the exact string Enable), so the danger is not forgetting to set it, it is a tutorial or a helpful agent turning it on. If the user genuinely wants anonymous submissions, make them say yes to that specific sentence, set CHHOTO_PUBLIC_MODE_EXPIRY_DELAY so submitted links expire, and tell them that abuse is a support@redu.cloud conversation rather than a silent one."
21	  - "⛔ SQLITE ON A VOLUME IS THE ONLY STORAGE THERE IS, SO THE VOLUME IS THE WHOLE DATABASE. There is no Postgres option and no managed database on this bill; do NOT pass database:'managed', because nothing in this stack speaks SQL over a network. With no CHHOTO_DB_URL the default is already /data/urls.sqlite and config.rs:64-104 creates the directory, so the app comes up perfectly healthy with the database inside the container's writable layer if you forget the volume, and every shortlink dies at the next redeploy while nothing warns you. PROVE IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because an absence alone proves nothing: positive half first, which is also what tells you your command worked at all, run `sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /data` and confirm urls.sqlite is there; THEN run `sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' <container>` and confirm /data is a named VOLUME rather than nothing, and `sudo ls /var/lib/docker/volumes/<project>_data/_data` on the VM and confirm the same file is visible from the host. If the first command errors, the later output means nothing. ⚠️ The exec only works because this recipe pins the -alpine image; see the next quirk."
22	  - "⛔ PIN THE -alpine IMAGE, DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE THE DEFAULT ONE HAS NO SHELL. docs/INSTALLATION.md says the default images are built FROM scratch and the -alpine ones add basic Unix tools. Consequences you will hit: docker exec cannot run ls, cat or anything else on a scratch image, so the database proof above is impossible; and upstream's own healthcheck, which they ship commented out, uses wget and therefore only works on alpine. Their own comment says so. Pin sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine (published 2026-07-24, matching the GitHub release, one of 202 tags on Docker Hub). ⚠️ latest and scratch are synonyms and so are latest-alpine and alpine, all of them rolling. dev tags are published to GHCR only and INSTALLATION.md says in bold not to use them for production. Never write a rolling tag into a recipe."
23	  - "ENABLE WAL MODE, WHICH IS THE THING THE BROKEN LINE IN THEIR COMPOSE WAS TRYING TO DO. Set CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE to the exact string True (any other value is ignored). Upstream marks it as one of the important options and recommends it in both the README and INSTALLATION.md: writes stop blocking reads. The condition attached to it is the one this recipe already satisfies, namely that the database must sit in a mounted DIRECTORY or named volume and never be a single bind-mounted FILE, because a bare file mount carries a small but real chance of partial data loss in WAL mode. Leave CHHOTO_SQLITE_ENSURE_ACID alone: ACID is the default and turning it off buys throughput this workload will never need."
24	  - "⛔ GENERATE A LONG API KEY OR THE APP PRINTS IT INTO THE LOGS. Verified in config.rs:167-177: at boot it scores the key, and if it scores under 90 it logs AT WARN LEVEL the current key in plaintext alongside a generated replacement, and then carries on using the weak one. So a short key ends up in the container log and in the deploy build log, where it is far easier to read than to rotate. Upstream's own suggestion is 128 characters from A-Za-z0-9. Generate it alphanumeric-only so there is nothing to escape in JSON or a shell, pass it as CHHOTO_API_KEY, and hand it to the user in the session rather than writing it anywhere. Without an API key the site still works, but the CLI and the JSON API are a significantly worse experience, per INSTALLATION.md."
25	  - "SET CHHOTO_SITE_URL, AND THEREFORE GENERATE THE DNAME UP FRONT. Shortlinks resolve at whatever URL the app is reachable on, so this is not load-bearing for redirects; it IS what the frontend uses for copy-to-clipboard and QR code generation, and config.rs falls back to http://localhost with an info line when it is unset, which is what a user sees when they click copy. Generate the dname yourself in full `chhoto-url-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form so the value is known before first boot; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Pass it as https://<that host>, with no quotes around it and no trailing slash."
26	  - "PORT 4567, AND redu's TLS IS DOING REAL WORK HERE. The app listens on 0.0.0.0:4567 by default (CHHOTO_LISTEN_ADDRESS and CHHOTO_LISTEN_PORT change it; do not). Publish 4567 and pass 4567 to deploy_compose. The README says in its own words that the password is not encrypted in transport and recommends a reverse proxy to encrypt the connection: redu terminates TLS on the *.redu.cloud hostname, so that requirement is met by the platform rather than by anything you configure. Never expose this app over plain HTTP."
27	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ONCE A PASSWORD IS SET, READ FROM THE ROUTE HANDLERS RATHER THAN GUESSED: the login page, every existing shortlink (which is the entire point of the app), GET /api/version, GET /api/siteurl (so your configured site URL is public) and GET /api/whoami, which answers the single word nobody. GET /api/all is 401 and GET /api/getconfig is 401 unless public mode is on. That is the whole anonymous surface. ⚠️ Shortlinks themselves are not secrets in any mode: adjective-name slugs like gifted-ramanujan are enumerable in practice by anyone willing to guess. If the user shortens anything they would not want a stranger to stumble onto, set CHHOTO_SLUG_STYLE to UID and CHHOTO_SLUG_LENGTH to 16 or more, which upstream also recommends past a few thousand links. This recipe leaves the default Pair style; it is a decision to put to the user, not one to make silently."
28	  - "OPTIONAL HARDENING, WITH A COMPOSE TRAP ATTACHED: CHHOTO_HASH_ALGORITHM=Argon2 lets you supply an Argon2 hash instead of the plaintext password and API key, so the secret is not sitting in the container environment where anything that can inspect the container can read it. Their recommended hashing command is in INSTALLATION.md. ⚠️ The hash contains dollar signs, and a dollar sign in a compose file is interpolation: it must be doubled to escape it, which upstream's compose comment says explicitly. Getting that wrong produces a hash that silently does not match and a password that never works. It also adds latency to every authenticated request. Worth it for a long-lived instance, and skip it on a first deploy if you want one fewer thing to get wrong."
29	  - "BACKUPS EXIST AND THEY LIVE ON THE SAME VOLUME, WHICH IS BOTH GOOD NEWS AND THE CAVEAT. Per INSTALLATION.md the app writes a backup at init and daily between 3am and 4am into a backups directory beside the database file, keeping 3 init and 7 daily copies and purging the rest. So the volume this recipe mounts holds the live database and its history. It is NOT off-VM: delete_deployment destroys the VM and the volume together, and there is no managed database here that outlives the deployment. If the links matter, copy the volume off the VM before tearing anything down, and say that out loud before you delete."
30	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. Checked the README, docs/INSTALLATION.md, the compose file and the Containerfiles: there is no memory figure anywhere. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB, 20 GB disk) is reasoning from 'one static Rust binary from a musl target plus a SQLite file, no interpreter and no database process', not a measurement. It fits the no-card free trial. Disk grows with the number of links, which is bytes per link, plus the ten retained backup copies. Measure the real idle figure on your run and write it back."
31	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate the dname yourself and a long alphanumeric admin password and a 128-character alphanumeric API key -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.017/hr, roughly GBP 13 a month, with no database on the bill because the app uses SQLite on a volume; fits the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), port 4567, and NO database parameter -> run the verification script in the body of this file BEFORE handing over the URL. plan_deploy wants to upsize a compose stack to m1.large, which is the right default for things that BUILD from source and wrong here, since the image is pulled: passing flavor_id '2' holds m1.small."
32	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source. Write the corrected docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
33	  - "LICENCE: plain MIT, verified by reading the whole 21-line LICENSE file (Copyright 2023-2026 Sayantan Santra), with no addendum, no Commons Clause and no network clause. Nothing constrains a self-hoster beyond retaining the notice. The repository carries SPDX headers throughout, so if you redistribute a modified build, keep them. MIT grants no trademark rights, so do not rebrand and redistribute under the Chhoto URL name."

140	#!/usr/bin/env bash
141	# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
142	#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
143	# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
144	set -eu
145	HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
146	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
147	
148	# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
149	# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
150	SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass
151	
152	inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }
153	
154	# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
155	#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
156	#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
157	code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
158	if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
159	  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
160	fi
161	if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
162	  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
163	fi
164	if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
165	  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
166	fi
167	echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"
168	
169	# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
170	#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
171	code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
172	if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
173	  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
174	fi
175	case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
176	  nobody)
177	    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
178	    ;;
179	  admin)
180	    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
181	    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
182	    exit 1
183	    ;;
184	  public)
185	    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
186	    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
187	    ;;
188	  *)
189	    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
190	    ;;
191	esac
192	
193	# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
194	#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
195	#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
196	code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
197	  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
198	case "$code" in
199	  401)
200	    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
201	    exit 0
202	    ;;
203	  200)
204	    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
205	    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
206	    exit 1
207	    ;;
208	  404|405)
209	    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
210	  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
211	    ;;
212	  *)
213	    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
214	    ;;
215	esac

# Self-host Chhoto URL on redu

```bash
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac
```

input.redu_md:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/SinTan1729/chhoto-url
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
  port: 4567
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none. This app stores its links in SQLite on a volume and speaks no other database; deploy_compose already defaults to database 'compose', which is correct here
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: chhoto-url
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ UPSTREAM'S SHIPPED compose.yaml DOES NOT PARSE. DO NOT COPY IT. Two separate defects, both measured by running docker compose config against the committed file (Docker 29.6.2, 2026-08-17), and either one alone stops the stack before a single image is pulled. FIRST: the WAL option is written with spaces around the equals sign, which makes the variable NAME carry a trailing space; compose refuses the file with 'environment variable CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE  is declared with a trailing space'. On any engine lenient enough to accept it, the app would look for a name it never sees and WAL mode would be silently off, which is the worse outcome of the two. SECOND, after fixing that: 'service chhoto-url refers to undefined volume data: invalid compose project', because the service mounts data:/data while the top-level volumes block declares db. Use the corrected compose written out in the body of this file, and write environment as a MAP rather than a list of strings so this whole class of bug cannot recur."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. THE ADMINISTRATOR IS WHOEVER KNOWS CHHOTO_PASSWORD, AND YOU SET IT AT DEPLOY TIME. That is the safe-by-construction case, so there is no first-visitor race to lose. It is also the ONLY thing standing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. The API will be accessible to the public.' GENERATE A LONG ALPHANUMERIC PASSWORD, pass it as CHHOTO_PASSWORD, and verify with the whoami check in the body of this file BEFORE handing over the URL. # Self-host Chhoto URL on redu

A URL shortener with no bloat: one small Rust binary, a SQLite file, a public HTTPS URL and one
password. No accounts, no tracking, no newsletter popups, because upstream refuses to build them.

About GBP 0.017/hour, roughly GBP 13 a month. There is no managed database on the bill, because
the links live in SQLite on a volume. Inside the no-card free trial.

## Read this before you deploy

**A shortener on a public hostname is a phishing tool if anyone else can post to it.** Chhoto URL
has no destination screening at all, by design. Keep public mode off, keep the admin password
strong, and understand that abuse gets the hostname blocklisted, which is a shared cost.

**There are no accounts, only a password.** One password and one API key run the whole instance,
forever: upstream's README lists user management under "bloat that will not be implemented". That
is a feature for a single-owner shortener and a hard stop if you needed per-user access.

## What this deploys

- **Chhoto URL** from the official image, pinned to the `-alpine` variant, on one m1.small VM,
  port 4567.
- **A volume on `/data`** holding `urls.sqlite`, its WAL files and the backups the app takes
  itself.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, which this app genuinely needs: upstream says
  plainly that the password is not encrypted in transport.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Chhoto URL on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The compose, because upstream's does not parse

Their committed `deploy/compose.yaml` fails `docker compose config` twice over: the WAL option
is written with spaces around the `=`, which makes the variable name carry a trailing space, and
the service mounts a volume named `data` while the top-level block declares one named `db`.
Neither reaches the point of pulling an image. Use this instead, which writes `environment` as a
map so the first class of bug cannot recur:

```yaml
services:
  chhoto-url:
    image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    ports:
      - "4567:4567"
    environment:
      CHHOTO_DB_URL: "/data/urls.sqlite"
      CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE: "True"
      CHHOTO_SITE_URL: "${CHHOTO_SITE_URL}"
      CHHOTO_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_REDIRECT_METHOD: "TEMPORARY"
      CHHOTO_SLUG_STYLE: "Pair"
    volumes:
      - data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://localhost:4567/api/whoami || exit 1
      interval: 60s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 3
      timeout: 10s
volumes:
  data:
```

The three interpolated values are generated by you before deploying: the site URL is
`https://` plus a dname you generate in full `chhoto-url-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form,
the password is long and alphanumeric, and the API key is 128 alphanumeric characters.

The healthcheck is upstream's own, which they ship commented out because it needs `wget`. That
is one of the reasons this recipe pins the `-alpine` image rather than the default one, which is
built `FROM scratch` and contains no shell at all.

## Who becomes the administrator

**Whoever knows `CHHOTO_PASSWORD`, and you set it at deploy time.** There is no signup form, no
install wizard and no first-visitor race, which makes this the safe-by-construction case.

It is also the only thing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. In
`backend/src/auth.rs`, the session check opens with *"If there's no password provided, just
return true"*. An unset or empty password does not degrade the instance, it hands every anonymous
visitor an admin session. One warning line at boot is the entire signal.

**What an anonymous request can reach** once a password is set: the login page, every existing
shortlink, `/api/version`, `/api/siteurl` and `/api/whoami`. `/api/all` and
`/api/getconfig` are 401.

**Is registration open afterwards?** There is no registration, in any configuration. One password,
one API key, forever.

## Proving it is not wide open

Run this before you hand over the URL. It gates every assertion on proof that Chhoto URL is the
thing answering, then tests **behaviour** rather than configuration: an anonymous caller must be
told `nobody`, and upstream's published password must be refused.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac
```

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

content.text: Found a real defect. The healthcheck can never pass: `wget` resolves `localhost` to `[::1]`, but the app listens on IPv4 `0.0.0.0:4567` — connection refused, forever. `RestartCount=0`, so the app itself is fine and Docker won't restart on unhealthy, but the container will sit permanently `unhealthy` and lie to anything that gates on it. Fixing it to `127.0.0.1`.

input.redu_md:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/SinTan1729/chhoto-url
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
  port: 4567
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none. This app stores its links in SQLite on a volume and speaks no other database; deploy_compose already defaults to database 'compose', which is correct here
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: chhoto-url
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ UPSTREAM'S SHIPPED compose.yaml DOES NOT PARSE. DO NOT COPY IT. Two separate defects, both measured by running docker compose config against the committed file (Docker 29.6.2, 2026-08-17), and either one alone stops the stack before a single image is pulled. FIRST: the WAL option is written with spaces around the equals sign, which makes the variable NAME carry a trailing space; compose refuses the file with 'environment variable CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE  is declared with a trailing space'. On any engine lenient enough to accept it, the app would look for a name it never sees and WAL mode would be silently off, which is the worse outcome of the two. SECOND, after fixing that: 'service chhoto-url refers to undefined volume data: invalid compose project', because the service mounts data:/data while the top-level volumes block declares db. Use the corrected compose written out in the body of this file, and write environment as a MAP rather than a list of strings so this whole class of bug cannot recur."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THERE ARE NO ACCOUNTS. THE ADMINISTRATOR IS WHOEVER KNOWS CHHOTO_PASSWORD, AND YOU SET IT AT DEPLOY TIME. That is the safe-by-construction case, so there is no first-visitor race to lose. It is also the ONLY thing standing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. Verified in backend/src/auth.rs:112-115: is_session_valid begins 'If there's no password provided, just return true', so with an unset or empty password EVERY anonymous request is a valid admin session, with listing, editing and deletion. config.rs:221-226 filters an empty string out too, and the only signal is one warn line at boot, 'No password was provided. The API will be accessible to the public.' GENERATE A LONG ALPHANUMERIC PASSWORD, pass it as CHHOTO_PASSWORD, and verify with the whoami check in the body of this file BEFORE handing over the URL. There is no registration to close afterwards, ever: the README's 'Bloat that will not be implemented' section rules out user management by design."
  - "⛔ THE SHIPPED COMPOSE ALSO CARRIES A PUBLICLY DOCUMENTED PASSWORD, UNDER THE LEGACY VARIABLE NAME. Its environment block sets the old lowercase name to a value printed in their public repo, and that value still works: config.rs:41-51 falls back from CHHOTO_PASSWORD to the legacy lowercase name and merely warns 'consider updating your configs'. So a copy-paste deploy is an instance whose admin password is in a file anyone can read on GitHub. Use the NEW names (every variable is CHHOTO_-prefixed at 7.5.0) and your own generated value. The verification script in the body of this file probes the shipped one on purpose, because a wrong-password 401 is the only thing that proves your value is actually the one in force."
  - "⛔⛔ A URL SHORTENER ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS A SPAM AND PHISHING REDIRECT SERVICE THE MOMENT ANYONE ELSE CAN POST TO IT, AND THE COST LANDS ON THE HOSTNAME RATHER THAN ON WHOEVER ABUSED IT. Campaigns hunt for exactly this: an open shortener on a domain with a clean reputation. Within days the hostname is in Google Safe Browsing, the DNS blocklists and the corporate URL filters, and a *.redu.cloud name carries reputation other people share. Chhoto URL has NO destination screening of any kind: there is no blocklist, no reputation check and no report flow anywhere in the codebase, which is deliberate, since the README's own 'Bloat' section rules out that class of feature. So KEEP CHHOTO_PUBLIC_MODE OFF. It is off by default (config.rs reads it as enabled only on the exact string Enable), so the danger is not forgetting to set it, it is a tutorial or a helpful agent turning it on. If the user genuinely wants anonymous submissions, make them say yes to that specific sentence, set CHHOTO_PUBLIC_MODE_EXPIRY_DELAY so submitted links expire, and tell them that abuse is a support@redu.cloud conversation rather than a silent one."
  - "⛔ SQLITE ON A VOLUME IS THE ONLY STORAGE THERE IS, SO THE VOLUME IS THE WHOLE DATABASE. There is no Postgres option and no managed database on this bill; do NOT pass database:'managed', because nothing in this stack speaks SQL over a network. With no CHHOTO_DB_URL the default is already /data/urls.sqlite and config.rs:64-104 creates the directory, so the app comes up perfectly healthy with the database inside the container's writable layer if you forget the volume, and every shortlink dies at the next redeploy while nothing warns you. PROVE IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because an absence alone proves nothing: positive half first, which is also what tells you your command worked at all, run `sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /data` and confirm urls.sqlite is there; THEN run `sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' <container>` and confirm /data is a named VOLUME rather than nothing, and `sudo ls /var/lib/docker/volumes/<project>_data/_data` on the VM and confirm the same file is visible from the host. If the first command errors, the later output means nothing. ⚠️ The exec only works because this recipe pins the -alpine image; see the next quirk."
  - "⛔ PIN THE -alpine IMAGE, DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE THE DEFAULT ONE HAS NO SHELL. docs/INSTALLATION.md says the default images are built FROM scratch and the -alpine ones add basic Unix tools. Consequences you will hit: docker exec cannot run ls, cat or anything else on a scratch image, so the database proof above is impossible; and upstream's own healthcheck, which they ship commented out, uses wget and therefore only works on alpine. Their own comment says so. Pin sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine (published 2026-07-24, matching the GitHub release, one of 202 tags on Docker Hub). ⚠️ latest and scratch are synonyms and so are latest-alpine and alpine, all of them rolling. dev tags are published to GHCR only and INSTALLATION.md says in bold not to use them for production. Never write a rolling tag into a recipe."
  - "⛔ UPSTREAM'S HEALTHCHECK USES localhost AND THEREFORE NEVER PASSES. Measured on deploy 443 (2026-08-17): with their own `wget --spider http://localhost:4567/api/whoami`, every probe returns exit 1 with 'Connecting to localhost:4567 ([::1]:4567) / wget: can't connect to remote host: Connection refused'. busybox wget in the alpine image resolves localhost to the IPv6 [::1], while the app binds IPv4 0.0.0.0 only (the boot log says 'Listening address is set to 0.0.0.0'), so nothing is listening where the probe knocks. WRITE THE PROBE AS http://127.0.0.1:4567/api/whoami and it passes in one interval (verified: Health=healthy, FailingStreak=0). ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS NEARLY INVISIBLE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH A QUIRK: docker does NOT restart an unhealthy container without an orchestrator, so the app serves traffic perfectly and RestartCount stays 0 while the container sits permanently 'unhealthy'. redu's deploy goes ready and the site works, so nothing in the deploy output tells you. It only bites later, when something gates on health: a depends_on: service_healthy in a stack you grow into, an autoscaler, or a human reading docker ps and concluding the app is broken when it is not."
  - "ENABLE WAL MODE, WHICH IS THE THING THE BROKEN LINE IN THEIR COMPOSE WAS TRYING TO DO. Set CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE to the exact string True (any other value is ignored). Upstream marks it as one of the important options and recommends it in both the README and INSTALLATION.md: writes stop blocking reads. The condition attached to it is the one this recipe already satisfies, namely that the database must sit in a mounted DIRECTORY or named volume and never be a single bind-mounted FILE, because a bare file mount carries a small but real chance of partial data loss in WAL mode. Leave CHHOTO_SQLITE_ENSURE_ACID alone: ACID is the default and turning it off buys throughput this workload will never need. ✅ CONFIRM IT TOOK, because the setting is silently ignored on a typo: the boot log must say 'Using WAL journaling mode for database.' (deploy 443 did), and /data must show urls.sqlite-wal and urls.sqlite-shm beside urls.sqlite."
  - "⛔ GENERATE A LONG API KEY OR THE APP PRINTS IT INTO THE LOGS. Verified in config.rs:167-177: at boot it scores the key, and if it scores under 90 it logs AT WARN LEVEL the current key in plaintext alongside a generated replacement, and then carries on using the weak one. So a short key ends up in the container log and in the deploy build log, where it is far easier to read than to rotate. Upstream's own suggestion is 128 characters from A-Za-z0-9. Generate it alphanumeric-only so there is nothing to escape in JSON or a shell, pass it as CHHOTO_API_KEY, and hand it to the user in the session rather than writing it anywhere. Without an API key the site still works, but the CLI and the JSON API are a significantly worse experience, per INSTALLATION.md. ✅ A 128-char alphanumeric key logs the single line 'Secure API key was provided.' and nothing else; that line is your proof the key was NOT printed."
  - "SET CHHOTO_SITE_URL, AND THEREFORE GENERATE THE DNAME UP FRONT. Shortlinks resolve at whatever URL the app is reachable on, so this is not load-bearing for redirects; it IS what the frontend uses for copy-to-clipboard and QR code generation, and config.rs falls back to http://localhost with an info line when it is unset, which is what a user sees when they click copy. # Self-host Chhoto URL on redu

A URL shortener with no bloat: one small Rust binary, a SQLite file, a public HTTPS URL and one
password. No accounts, no tracking, no newsletter popups, because upstream refuses to build them.

About GBP 0.017/hour, roughly GBP 13 a month. There is no managed database on the bill, because
the links live in SQLite on a volume. Inside the no-card free trial.

## Read this before you deploy

**A shortener on a public hostname is a phishing tool if anyone else can post to it.** Chhoto URL
has no destination screening at all, by design. Keep public mode off, keep the admin password
strong, and understand that abuse gets the hostname blocklisted, which is a shared cost.

**There are no accounts, only a password.** One password and one API key run the whole instance,
forever: upstream's README lists user management under "bloat that will not be implemented". That
is a feature for a single-owner shortener and a hard stop if you needed per-user access.

## What this deploys

- **Chhoto URL** from the official image, pinned to the `-alpine` variant, on one m1.small VM,
  port 4567.
- **A volume on `/data`** holding `urls.sqlite`, its WAL files and the backups the app takes
  itself.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, which this app genuinely needs: upstream says
  plainly that the password is not encrypted in transport.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Chhoto URL on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The compose, because upstream's does not parse

Their committed `deploy/compose.yaml` fails `docker compose config` twice over: the WAL option
is written with spaces around the `=`, which makes the variable name carry a trailing space, and
the service mounts a volume named `data` while the top-level block declares one named `db`.
Neither reaches the point of pulling an image. Use this instead, which writes `environment` as a
map so the first class of bug cannot recur:

```yaml
services:
  chhoto-url:
    image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    ports:
      - "4567:4567"
    environment:
      CHHOTO_DB_URL: "/data/urls.sqlite"
      CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE: "True"
      CHHOTO_SITE_URL: "${CHHOTO_SITE_URL}"
      CHHOTO_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_REDIRECT_METHOD: "TEMPORARY"
      CHHOTO_SLUG_STYLE: "Pair"
    volumes:
      - data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # 127.0.0.1, NOT localhost: busybox wget resolves localhost to [::1] and the app binds
      # IPv4 0.0.0.0 only, so upstream's own healthcheck fails forever with "Connection refused".
      test: wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://127.0.0.1:4567/api/whoami || exit 1
      interval: 60s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 3
      timeout: 10s
volumes:
  data:
```

The three interpolated values are generated by you before deploying: the site URL is
`https://` plus a dname you generate in full `chhoto-url-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form,
the password is long and alphanumeric, and the API key is 128 alphanumeric characters.

The healthcheck is upstream's own, which they ship commented out because it needs `wget`, with
one correction: their version probes `localhost`, which busybox `wget` resolves to `[::1]` while
the app binds IPv4 only, so it fails on every interval forever. `127.0.0.1` passes immediately.
The `wget` dependency is one of the reasons this recipe pins the `-alpine` image rather than the
default one, which is built `FROM scratch` and contains no shell at all.

## Who becomes the administrator

**Whoever knows `CHHOTO_PASSWORD`, and you set it at deploy time.** There is no signup form, no
install wizard and no first-visitor race, which makes this the safe-by-construction case.

It is also the only thing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. In
`backend/src/auth.rs`, the session check opens with *"If there's no password provided, just
return true"*. An unset or empty password does not degrade the instance, it hands every anonymous
visitor an admin session. One warning line at boot is the entire signal.

**What an anonymous request can reach** once a password is set: the login page, every existing
shortlink, `/api/version`, `/api/siteurl` and `/api/whoami`. `/api/all` and
`/api/getconfig` are 401.

**Is registration open afterwards?** There is no registration, in any configuration. One password,
one API key, forever.

## Proving it is not wide open

Run this before you hand over the URL. It gates every assertion on proof that Chhoto URL is the
thing answering, then tests **behaviour** rather than configuration: an anonymous caller must be
told `nobody`, and upstream's published password must be refused.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac
```

# Self-host Chhoto URL on redu

A URL shortener with no bloat: one small Rust binary, a SQLite file, a public HTTPS URL and one
password. No accounts, no tracking, no newsletter popups, because upstream refuses to build them.

About GBP 0.017/hour, roughly GBP 13 a month. There is no managed database on the bill, because
the links live in SQLite on a volume. Inside the no-card free trial.

## Read this before you deploy

**A shortener on a public hostname is a phishing tool if anyone else can post to it.** Chhoto URL
has no destination screening at all, by design. Keep public mode off, keep the admin password
strong, and understand that abuse gets the hostname blocklisted, which is a shared cost.

**There are no accounts, only a password.** One password and one API key run the whole instance,
forever: upstream's README lists user management under "bloat that will not be implemented". That
is a feature for a single-owner shortener and a hard stop if you needed per-user access.

## What this deploys

- **Chhoto URL** from the official image, pinned to the `-alpine` variant, on one m1.small VM,
  port 4567.
- **A volume on `/data`** holding `urls.sqlite`, its WAL files and the backups the app takes
  itself.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, which this app genuinely needs: upstream says
  plainly that the password is not encrypted in transport.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Chhoto URL on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The compose, because upstream's does not parse

Their committed `deploy/compose.yaml` fails `docker compose config` twice over: the WAL option
is written with spaces around the `=`, which makes the variable name carry a trailing space, and
the service mounts a volume named `data` while the top-level block declares one named `db`.
Neither reaches the point of pulling an image. Use this instead, which writes `environment` as a
map so the first class of bug cannot recur:

```yaml
services:
  chhoto-url:
    image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    ports:
      - "4567:4567"
    environment:
      CHHOTO_DB_URL: "/data/urls.sqlite"
      CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE: "True"
      CHHOTO_SITE_URL: "${CHHOTO_SITE_URL}"
      CHHOTO_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_REDIRECT_METHOD: "TEMPORARY"
      CHHOTO_SLUG_STYLE: "Pair"
    volumes:
      - data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # 127.0.0.1, NOT localhost: busybox wget resolves localhost to [::1] and the app binds
      # IPv4 0.0.0.0 only, so upstream's own healthcheck fails forever with "Connection refused".
      test: wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://127.0.0.1:4567/api/whoami || exit 1
      interval: 60s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 3
      timeout: 10s
volumes:
  data:
```

The three interpolated values are generated by you before deploying: the site URL is
`https://` plus a dname you generate in full `chhoto-url-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form,
the password is long and alphanumeric, and the API key is 128 alphanumeric characters.

The healthcheck is upstream's own, which they ship commented out because it needs `wget`, with
one correction found on the first real deploy: their version probes `localhost`, which busybox
`wget` resolves to `[::1]` while the app binds IPv4 only, so it fails on every interval forever
without ever restarting or degrading the app. `127.0.0.1` passes on the first probe. The `wget`
dependency is one of the reasons this recipe pins the `-alpine` image rather than the default
one, which is built `FROM scratch` and contains no shell at all.

## Who becomes the administrator

**Whoever knows `CHHOTO_PASSWORD`, and you set it at deploy time.** There is no signup form, no
install wizard and no first-visitor race, which makes this the safe-by-construction case.

It is also the only thing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. In
`backend/src/auth.rs`, the session check opens with *"If there's no password provided, just
return true"*. An unset or empty password does not degrade the instance, it hands every anonymous
visitor an admin session. One warning line at boot is the entire signal.

**What an anonymous request can reach** once a password is set: the login page, every existing
shortlink, `/api/version`, `/api/siteurl` and `/api/whoami`. `/api/all` and
`/api/getconfig` are 401.

**Is registration open afterwards?** There is no registration, in any configuration. One password,
one API key, forever.

## Proving it is not wide open

Run this before you hand over the URL. It gates every assertion on proof that Chhoto URL is the
thing answering, then tests **behaviour** rather than configuration: an anonymous caller must be
told `nobody`, and upstream's published password must be refused.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac
```

This file ships that script as `verify-chhoto.sh` beside it. Note that a run of it leaves one
`WARN Failed login attempt!` line in the container log — that is step 3's negative control being
refused, which is the pass condition, not an intrusion.

```bash
sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' app-src-chhoto-url-1

# health is genuinely green rather than permanently starting
sudo docker inspect -f 'Health={{.State.Health.Status}} Fails={{.State.Health.FailingStreak}}' app-src-chhoto-url-1
```

# Self-host Chhoto URL on redu

A URL shortener with no bloat: one small Rust binary, a SQLite file, a public HTTPS URL and one
password. No accounts, no tracking, no newsletter popups, because upstream refuses to build them.

About GBP 0.017/hour, roughly GBP 13 a month. There is no managed database on the bill, because
the links live in SQLite on a volume. Inside the no-card free trial.

## Read this before you deploy

**A shortener on a public hostname is a phishing tool if anyone else can post to it.** Chhoto URL
has no destination screening at all, by design. Keep public mode off, keep the admin password
strong, and understand that abuse gets the hostname blocklisted, which is a shared cost.

**There are no accounts, only a password.** One password and one API key run the whole instance,
forever: upstream's README lists user management under "bloat that will not be implemented". That
is a feature for a single-owner shortener and a hard stop if you needed per-user access.

## What this deploys

- **Chhoto URL** from the official image, pinned to the `-alpine` variant, on one m1.small VM,
  port 4567.
- **A volume on `/data`** holding `urls.sqlite`, its WAL files and the backups the app takes
  itself.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS, which this app genuinely needs: upstream says
  plainly that the password is not encrypted in transport.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Chhoto URL on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The compose, because upstream's does not parse

Their committed `deploy/compose.yaml` fails `docker compose config` twice over: the WAL option
is written with spaces around the `=`, which makes the variable name carry a trailing space, and
the service mounts a volume named `data` while the top-level block declares one named `db`.
Neither reaches the point of pulling an image. Use this instead, which writes `environment` as a
map so the first class of bug cannot recur:

```yaml
services:
  chhoto-url:
    image: sintan1729/chhoto-url:7.5.0-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    tty: true
    ports:
      - "4567:4567"
    environment:
      CHHOTO_DB_URL: "/data/urls.sqlite"
      CHHOTO_SQLITE_USE_WAL_MODE: "True"
      CHHOTO_SITE_URL: "${CHHOTO_SITE_URL}"
      CHHOTO_PASSWORD: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_API_KEY: "[REDACTED:value]}"
      CHHOTO_REDIRECT_METHOD: "TEMPORARY"
      CHHOTO_SLUG_STYLE: "Pair"
    volumes:
      - data:/data
    healthcheck:
      # 127.0.0.1, NOT localhost: busybox wget resolves localhost to [::1] and the app binds
      # IPv4 0.0.0.0 only, so upstream's own healthcheck fails forever with "Connection refused".
      test: wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://127.0.0.1:4567/api/whoami || exit 1
      interval: 60s
      start_period: 10s
      retries: 3
      timeout: 10s
volumes:
  data:
```

The three interpolated values are generated by you before deploying: the site URL is
`https://` plus a dname you generate in full `chhoto-url-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form,
the password is long and alphanumeric, and the API key is 128 alphanumeric characters.

The healthcheck is upstream's own, which they ship commented out because it needs `wget`, with
one correction found on the first real deploy: their version probes `localhost`, which busybox
`wget` resolves to `[::1]` while the app binds IPv4 only, so it fails on every interval forever
without ever restarting or degrading the app. `127.0.0.1` passes on the first probe. The `wget`
dependency is one of the reasons this recipe pins the `-alpine` image rather than the default
one, which is built `FROM scratch` and contains no shell at all.

## Who becomes the administrator

**Whoever knows `CHHOTO_PASSWORD`, and you set it at deploy time.** There is no signup form, no
install wizard and no first-visitor race, which makes this the safe-by-construction case.

It is also the only thing between the internet and full control, and the failure is silent. In
`backend/src/auth.rs`, the session check opens with *"If there's no password provided, just
return true"*. An unset or empty password does not degrade the instance, it hands every anonymous
visitor an admin session. One warning line at boot is the entire signal.

**What an anonymous request can reach** once a password is set: the login page, every existing
shortlink, `/api/version`, `/api/siteurl` and `/api/whoami`. `/api/all` and
`/api/getconfig` are 401.

**Is registration open afterwards?** There is no registration, in any configuration. One password,
one API key, forever.

## Proving it is not wide open

Run this before you hand over the URL. It gates every assertion on proof that Chhoto URL is the
thing answering, then tests **behaviour** rather than configuration: an anonymous caller must be
told `nobody`, and upstream's published password must be refused.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove this Chhoto URL is serving and is not anonymously administrable.
#   ./verify-chhoto.sh chhoto-url-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
# Exit 0 = locked, 1 = OPEN (fix it now), 2 = inconclusive (it may still be starting).
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-chhoto.sh <host>}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# The password upstream's compose.yaml ships. Not a secret: [REDACTED:value] is committed in their public repo,
# which is exactly why an instance that still accepts it is an instance anyone can administer.
SHIPPED_PW=TopSecretPass

inconclusive() { echo "INCONCLUSIVE: $1" >&2; exit 2; }

# 1. GATE plus POSITIVE CONTROL in one call. redu's hostname answers 502 from its proxy for
#    roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the container starts, and an error page passes every
#    "did it NOT do X" check below by accident. /api/version is anonymous and app-specific.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/ver" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/version")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered 502. That is redu's proxy while the container starts, NOT a pass. Re-run."
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/version answered HTTP $code, not 200."
fi
if ! grep -q 'Chhoto URL v' "$TMP/ver"; then
  inconclusive "/api/version returned 200 but its body is not Chhoto URL's."
fi
echo "OK: Chhoto URL is serving, version: $(cat "$TMP/ver")"

# 2. THE ASSERTION. An anonymous caller must be told "nobody". "admin" means no password is in
#    force and the whole instance is administrable by anyone who finds it.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/who" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/whoami")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  inconclusive "/api/whoami answered HTTP $code, not 200, so this probe proved nothing."
fi
case "$(cat "$TMP/who")" in
  nobody)
    echo "OK: an anonymous caller is nobody."
    ;;
  admin)
    echo "FAIL: an ANONYMOUS caller is admin. No password is in force, so anyone who finds this" >&2
    echo "URL can list, edit and delete every link. Set CHHOTO_PASSWORD and redeploy now." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  public)
    echo "WARNING: public mode is ON, so anyone can create shortlinks here. That makes the" >&2
    echo "hostname a spam and phishing target. Confirm this was deliberate." >&2
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "/api/whoami returned something this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac

# 3. NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE CREDENTIAL ITSELF. Step 2 only proves SOME password is required.
#    This proves it is not the one committed in upstream's repo. The body IS the password, so it
#    goes on stdin: an argument would show up in ps for every user on the machine.
code=$(printf '%s' "$SHIPPED_PW" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -X POST --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/login")
case "$code" in
  401)
    echo "OK: upstream's published password is refused, so your own value is in force."
    exit 0
    ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the instance accepted the password committed in upstream's compose file." >&2
    echo "Anyone who has read their repo is an administrator here. Regenerate and redeploy." >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  404|405)
    inconclusive "POST /api/login answered HTTP $code, so the route has moved and this probe
  proved nothing. Do not leave this instance up until you have checked it by hand."
    ;;
  *)
    inconclusive "the login probe answered HTTP $code, which this script does not recognise."
    ;;
esac
```

This file ships that script as `verify-chhoto.sh` beside it. Note that a run of it leaves one
`WARN Failed login attempt!` line in the container log — that is step 3's negative control being
refused, which is the pass condition, not an intrusion.

## Checking the deploy from the VM

The three things worth reading once, none of which the deploy output tells you:

```bash
# WAL actually on, site URL matches, API key not printed
sudo docker logs app-src-chhoto-url-1 2>&1 | head -30
# the database is on the named volume, not the container's writable layer
sudo docker exec app-src-chhoto-url-1 ls -l /data
sudo docker inspect -f '{{json .Mounts}}' app-src-chhoto-url-1
sudo ls -l /var/lib/docker/volumes/app-src_data/_data
# health is genuinely green rather than permanently starting
sudo docker inspect -f 'Health={{.State.Health.Status}} Fails={{.State.Health.FailingStreak}}' app-src-chhoto-url-1
```
